summary.GET: Accounts with balances (integer hundredths in each account's own currency; a parent's balance is null), sub-accounts nested. Args: include_hidden (false), category, currency, with_sub_accounts (true), name (flat rows, exact then case-insensitive).
summary.POST: Create an account. Body: name, category (cash, checking, savings, credit_card, virtual, debt, receivables, investment, certificate_of_deposit), currency (immutable later), initial_balance (hundredths; liabilities negative for money owed), initial_balance_date, color, icon, comment, credit_card_statement_date, credit_card_limit, sub_accounts: [{name, currency, initial_balance, initial_balance_date, color, icon, comment}], idempotency_key; dry_run default true.

summary.DELETE: Delete an account with its sub-accounts and opening balances; refused while transactions or templates use it, naming the count.
summary.GET: One account (id or name; sub-accounts too) with its sub-accounts or parent name.
summary.PATCH: Edit an account or sub-account. Body: name, color, icon, comment, credit_card_statement_date, credit_card_limit. Currency and category are immutable here.

summary.GET: One account's balance as of a date (default today), composed from the daily asset trend.
One account's closing balance over time (day, week or month).

summary.POST: Hide or show an account. Body: hidden (default true).
Reorder an account among its siblings (same category, or same parent). Body: to_index (0-based).

summary.GET: Transaction count, first/last transaction, last reconciled time, credit-card statement date and limit, and the opening-balance rows.

summary.POST: Mark the account reconciled; with create_adjustment, first add ONE visible adjustment for the difference.
The app's balance as of a date against the operator's figure, the difference, and the rows since the last reconciliation; returns the confirm_token for apply.

summary.GET: Upstream's reconciliation statement: opening, inflows, outflows, closing, per-row running balance.

summary.DELETE: Delete one sub-account (never the last one); refused while transactions or templates use it.

summary.POST: Create many accounts in order under one token; on a failure the ones already created are removed again and the failing index is named. Body: accounts: [create bodies].
Clear data (dry_run default): scope all | transactions | transactions_of_account (with account_id). Not undoable. Body: {scope, account_id?, dry_run, confirm_token, max_changes}.
Mint a new API secret key into the credentials file (dry_run default). Answers fingerprints only; the running server keeps the old key until it is restarted (ezbk stop && ezbk up).

summary.DELETE: Remove transaction pictures uploaded but never attached (dry_run default). Body: {ids?, older_than_days? (default 1), dry_run, confirm_token, max_changes}.

summary.GET: The bound user's upstream sessions and API/MCP tokens: id, type, user agent, last seen. Never a token value.

summary.DELETE: Revoke one upstream session or token (dry_run default). An id already gone answers ok with deleted: 0.

summary.GET: Categories unusually far from their own trailing monthly norm, with the evidence.
Opening balance, money in, money out and closing balance per interval, for a set of accounts.
One category (with its sub-categories) over time, with mean and median.
Rows an import placed in its fallback category, by account and month, so they can be re-categorised.
Income by primary or secondary category (or account), per interval, with top_n and an 'other' bucket.
Income, expense and net per interval (day, week, month, quarter, year).
Assets, liabilities and net worth per interval, and each account's closing balance.
Who got the money, grouped by normalised transaction comment (ezBookkeeping has no payee entity), with the raw variants merged.
Income and expense per named period (today, this_week, this_month, this_year, last_month, custom …), per currency — the Overview page.
Detected repeating charges (and income) not yet scheduled, their cadence, evidence and annualised cost.
Liquid assets divided by the trailing average monthly net outflow, in months.
Expense by primary or secondary category (or account), per interval, with top_n and an 'other' bucket — the pie / bar chart.
Spending and income per tag — what the trip cost.

Passthrough: any upstream GET /api/v1/<path> as the bound user; data is upstream's result verbatim (amounts stay upstream's strings). tokens/*, users/2fa/*, users/external_auth/*, users/avatar/*, users/verify_email/*, llm/* are refused.
summary.POST: Passthrough: any upstream POST /api/v1/<path> as the bound user, with NO dry run, confirm token, ceiling or journal. */delete.json, */batch_delete.json, data/clear/*, */remove_unused.json need the admin tier; tokens/*, users/2fa/*, users/external_auth/*, users/avatar/*, users/verify_email/*, llm/* are refused.

Apply an ordered list of write operations under one confirm token, one ceiling (counting changes, not operations) and one journal entry; on the first failure the applied ones are reversed through the journal and the response says rolledBack. Body: {operations: [{op: "METHOD /path", params?, query?, args?}], dry_run, confirm_token, max_changes}. GET /batch/ops lists the closed op set.

summary.GET: The closed set of operations POST /batch accepts (every live, dry-runnable write-tier route).
The machine-readable route table of this build.

Categories, primaries with secondaries nested. Args: type (income|expense|transfer), include_hidden (false), parent_id (id or name → its children, flat), name (exact, then case-insensitive → flat rows), flat.
summary.POST: Create a category. Body: name, type (omit under a parent), parent_id|parent_name (omit for a primary), color, icon, comment, idempotency_key; dry_run default true.

summary.DELETE: Delete a category and its secondaries; refused while transactions or templates use it, naming the count.
summary.GET: One category (id or name), with its secondaries when primary.
summary.PATCH: Edit a category. Body: name, parent_id|parent_name (secondaries only, same type), color, icon, comment.

summary.POST: Hide or show a category. Body: hidden (default true).
Reorder a category among its siblings (same type and parent). Body: to_index (0-based).
Create primaries with their secondaries (the web UI's default-categories preset). Body: categories: [{name, type, color, icon, comment, sub_categories: [{name, color, icon, comment}]}].

summary.GET: Upstream's ezBookkeeping-format export as a raw file. Args: format (csv|tsv), start, end (YYYY-MM-DD).
Counts of accounts, categories, tags, transactions, pictures, templates, schedules, insights and custom icons.

The app's latest exchange rates (units per ONE base-currency unit), each with source (provider|custom), provider and updateTime, plus the stored custom rates and whether upstream uses them. Args: currencies (list).

summary.POST: Convert an amount with the app's own rates. Body: amount (hundredths), from, to. Returns converted (hundredths), the rate used, both source rates with their source and updateTime, rateBasis latest.

summary.DELETE: Remove a custom rate (a preference, not a record — write tier). Not set is ok with deleted: 0.
summary.PUT: Set a custom rate: rate = units of :currency per ONE unit of the user's default currency (a decimal). Used by upstream only when [exchange_rates] data_source = user_custom; the preview says so.

summary.GET: Database open? user bindable? upstream doors on? what to do next.

summary.POST: Create the plan's create rows, link the link rows and write the map (confirm_token from /ingest/accounts/plan, dry_run). Ambiguous rows are never created. Undoable.

Plan the accounts from the manifest (root, naming, kind_to_category, overrides, accounts[]): per row create/link/skip/ambiguous with the category, its asset/liability side and the currency read aloud. Creates nothing; returns the confirm_token for /ingest/accounts/apply.

Import the plan (confirm_token, max_changes, dry_run; or the plan's arguments again). Recomputes the plan and refuses on a moved fingerprint; creates through upstream's import service path; records machine_import_record; undoable. NDJSON progress with Accept: application/x-ndjson.

summary.GET: The fileTypes this build's pkg/converters supports, which are enabled, which carry bank ids, and what each needs (qif date order, column map).
Which account-months are present and which are missing (root, account, manifest_path, from_rows).
What both de-duplication layers collapsed, and why (root, mode, account, prefer, date_order): duplicate_identical, superseded (with the deciding rule), conflicts, same-bank-id collapses.

summary.POST: RAW MODE ONLY. Read-tier but WRITES to the staging directory only: produce ezBookkeeping CSV per account-month from _claude/_brew/_ocr sidecars with a conservative line parser (root, force, date_order, accounts[], prefer[], max_statements). Zero-row statements are named. NDJSON progress with Accept: application/x-ndjson.
Import one planned file (confirm_token, dry_run, max_changes). Undoable.

The Import dialog for one file: account_id (or account_name), path under the root OR multipart field "file", file_type, column_map for custom files; category_map, fallback_category_ids, accept_matches[]. Returns the plan and the confirm_token for /ingest/file/apply.

summary.GET: Read the archive's manifest (root, manifest_path): per account the converter the plane will use, combined/monthly files, formats, warnings; missing columns reported, never guessed.
The statements→books map (root): each account key's ezBookkeeping account and whether it is still usable; manifest accounts not yet mapped.
summary.PUT: Write the statements→books map beside the statements ({ROOT}/.ezbk-staging/_map.json, never the repo). Args: root, map {account_key: account_id}, replace, dry_run, confirm_token. Undoable.

summary.POST: Propose account mappings for the manifest (root, manifest_path): map, exact name, last4; never saves.

Plan the import of a statements root (root, accounts[], start, end, category_map, fallback_category_ids, accept_matches[], accept_transfers[], reimport_deleted, prefer[], qif_date_order): per account parsed, collapsed, already present (and deleted since), possible matches, transfer candidates, unmapped, NEW; plus the confirm_token for /ingest/apply.

summary.GET: Configured statement roots, whether each is readable, its manifest and staging directory.
The de-duplicated statement rows with their import_id and their verdict against the books (root, account, start, end, status, limit, offset).
The ingest run log of the bound user, newest first (limit).
One run's full report: per-account outcome, unmapped categories, the rows that went to a fallback category, the journal entry that undoes it.

summary.POST: Walk the statements root and classify every file (root, mode, entity, institution, account, year, manifest_path): statements per account-year-month, missing months, duplicate scans, unusable files. Changes nothing.

summary.GET: Saved Insights Explorer definitions (not numbers — those come from /analytics). Args: include_hidden (false), name.
summary.POST: Save an insight definition. Body: name, definition (object), idempotency_key.

summary.GET: One saved insight (id or name) with its definition as data.
summary.PATCH: Rename an insight or replace its definition. Body: name, definition.

summary.POST: Hide or show an insight. Body: hidden (default true).
Reorder an insight. Body: to_index (0-based).

summary.GET: Recent machine-plane writes of the bound user: route, when, change counts, client, summary, undone? Never amounts. Args: limit, offset, include_undone.
Liveness, key fingerprint, tiers, server version.

summary.POST: Re-apply the most recently undone machine-plane write, available until a newer write lands. Body: {journal_id?}.

summary.GET: What the scheduled transactions will create in the window, computed with the cron's own calendar rule, firing nothing. Args: days (30), from (YYYY-MM-DD, default today), template_ids (ids or names), limit.
Tag groups with their tag counts. Args: name.
summary.POST: Create a tag group. Body: name, idempotency_key.

summary.DELETE: Delete an empty tag group; refused while it holds tags.
summary.GET: One tag group (id or name) with its tags.
summary.PATCH: Rename a tag group. Body: name.

summary.POST: Reorder a tag group. Body: to_index (0-based).

summary.GET: Tags. Args: include_hidden (false), group_id|group_name (0 = ungrouped), name.
summary.POST: Create a tag. Body: name, group_id|group_name, idempotency_key.

summary.DELETE: Delete a tag; refused while transactions or templates carry it, naming the count.
summary.GET: One tag (id or name), with how many transactions carry it.
summary.PATCH: Rename a tag or move it to another group. Body: name, group_id|group_name ("0" = no group).

summary.POST: Hide or show a tag. Body: hidden (default true).
Reorder a tag within its group. Body: to_index (0-based).
Create many tags in one group. Body: tags: ["name", …] or [{name}], group_id|group_name, skip_existing (true).

summary.GET: Transaction templates and scheduled transactions. Args: kind (normal|scheduled|all, default all), include_hidden (false), name.
summary.POST: Create a template (kind normal) or a scheduled transaction (kind scheduled). Body: kind, name, type, account_id|account_name, destination_account_id|destination_account_name, amount, destination_amount, category_id|category_name, tag_ids|tag_names, comment, hide_amount; scheduled: frequency (daily|weekly|monthly|yearly|every_n_days|disabled), frequency_value, start, end, timezone; idempotency_key.

summary.DELETE: Delete a template or schedule (transactions it already created are kept).
summary.GET: One template or schedule (id or name), with its next occurrence.
summary.PATCH: Edit a template or schedule: any create field; absent means unchanged; end "" removes the end date; frequency "disabled" pauses a schedule.

summary.POST: Hide or show a template. For a schedule this does NOT pause it (upstream's cron ignores hidden); the response says so. Body: hidden (default true).
Reorder a template among its kind. Body: to_index (0-based).

summary.GET: Transactions matching the filters, newest first, walked through upstream's cursor up to limit (cap 5000); nextCursor pages on.
summary.POST: Add transactions (income, expense, transfer); names resolve to ids; dry run by default.

summary.DELETE: Delete one transaction (admin). Undo re-creates it with a new id.
summary.GET: One transaction, with its tags, pictures metadata and both sides of a transfer.
summary.PATCH: Edit one transaction; the preview is the exact field-by-field before/after.

summary.DELETE: Delete transactions by ids[] (admin). Undo re-creates them with new ids.

summary.GET: How many transactions match the filters (a transfer counts once).
The earliest transaction, optionally of one account.
The matching transactions as upstream's ezBookkeeping CSV or TSV.
The latest transaction, optionally of one account.

summary.POST: Move every transaction of one account to another account of the same currency.
Move transactions chosen by ids[] or filter{} to another account of the same currency.
Re-categorise transactions chosen by ids[] or by filter{} (the GET /transactions filter language).
Add tags to transactions chosen by ids[] or filter{}.
Remove every tag from transactions chosen by ids[] or filter{}.
Remove tags from transactions chosen by ids[] or filter{}.

Undo the most recent machine-plane write of the bound user (no dry_run: it returns what it reversed). Machine-plane writes only; a browser edit cannot be undone, and undo refuses with conflict when a row it would touch was edited since. Body: {journal_id?}.

summary.GET: The bound user's profile: nickname, default currency, first day of week, fiscal year start, display formats.
summary.PATCH: Change nickname, default_currency, first_day_of_week (0-6 or name), fiscal_year_start (MM-DD), use_last_reconciled_time. Never password, email or avatar.

summary.GET: The web UI's synchronised application settings, with the allowed keys and their types.
summary.PATCH: Set one or more application settings. Body: settings: {key: value}; values are type-checked against allowedKeys.

summary.GET: Install, bound user, default currency, timezone, tiers, key fingerprint, statements root.
